statements.text: Brazil is the only country in the Americas where Portuguese is the main language.
Brazil has won the men's football World Cup five times, more than any other country.
Brazil's capital is Rio de Janeiro.
statements.truth: Brasília has been Brazil's capital since 1960. Rio de Janeiro was the capital before that.

statements.text: In parts of northern Norway, the sun doesn't set for weeks in the middle of summer.
Norway's coast is famous for its fjords, long narrow inlets carved out by glaciers.
Norway is a member of the European Union.
statements.truth: Norwegians voted against joining in 1972 and again in 1994. Norway works closely with the EU through the European Economic Area instead.

statements.text: Kenya is named after Mount Kenya, the second-highest mountain in Africa.
The equator runs through Kenya.
Kenya's capital is Mombasa.
statements.truth: Kenya's capital is Nairobi. Mombasa is its biggest port, on the Indian Ocean coast.

statements.text: All of China officially runs on a single time zone, despite the country's huge width.
Papermaking was invented in China around 2,000 years ago.
The Great Wall of China is easy to see from the Moon with the naked eye.
statements.truth: This is a popular myth. The wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon, and it's hard to spot even from low orbit.

statements.text: Iceland has no standing army.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest in the world.
More than half of Iceland is covered by glaciers.
statements.truth: Glaciers and lakes together cover only about 14% of Iceland. Much of the rest is highland, lava fields and tundra.

statements.text: Japan is made up of more than 14,000 islands.
Japan has more than 100 active volcanoes.
Japan's national flower is the lotus.
statements.truth: Japan has no national flower set in law, but the cherry blossom and the chrysanthemum are its traditional floral symbols.

statements.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still largely standing.
Most Egyptians live along the Nile and its delta.
The Nile flows south through Egypt toward the Red Sea.
statements.truth: The Nile flows north through Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

statements.text: Thailand is the only country in Southeast Asia that was never colonised by a Western power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
Thailand used to be called Burma.
statements.truth: Thailand was officially called Siam until 1939. Burma is the former name of neighbouring Myanmar.

statements.text: About half of the Netherlands is less than 1 m (3 ft) above sea level, and much of that is below it.
Amsterdam is the capital, but the government sits in The Hague.
Tulips are native to the Netherlands.
statements.truth: Wild tulips come from Central Asia and the region around Türkiye. They reached the Netherlands in the 1500s.

statements.text: Chile is more than 4,000 km (2,500 mi) long but on average less than 200 km (120 mi) wide.
Chile's Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth.
Easter Island is an independent country of its own.
statements.truth: Easter Island, also called Rapa Nui, is part of Chile.

statements.text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country.
English and French are both official languages of Canada's federal government.
Most Canadians live in the country's far north.
statements.truth: Most Canadians live in the south, many of them fairly close to the border with the United States.

statements.text: India has the largest population of any country.
Chess is widely believed to come from an ancient Indian game called chaturanga.
Hindi is India's only official language.
statements.truth: Hindi and English are both official languages of the central government, and the constitution recognises 22 scheduled languages.

statements.text: Morocco's al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is often called the oldest place of learning still in use.
At the Strait of Gibraltar, Morocco is only about 14 km (9 mi) from Spain.
Morocco's capital is Marrakesh.
statements.truth: Morocco's capital is Rabat. Casablanca is the biggest city, and Marrakesh is a famous historic city.

statements.text: Lake Baikal, in Siberia, is the deepest lake in the world.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world.
Russia's easternmost islands are more than 1,000 km from the nearest neighbouring country.
statements.truth: In the Bering Strait, Russia's Big Diomede Island and the United States' Little Diomede Island are less than 4 km (2.5 mi) apart.

statements.text: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world.
Wild lemurs live naturally only on Madagascar and a few small nearby islands.
Madagascar broke away from South America millions of years ago.
statements.truth: Madagascar separated from mainland Africa, and later from India, many millions of years ago.

statements.text: Two independent countries lie entirely inside Italy: San Marino and Vatican City.
The Po is Italy's longest river.
Pizza Margherita was named after a famous opera singer.
statements.truth: The usual story is that it was named after Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889.

statements.text: Indonesia is made up of more than 13,000 islands.
Komodo dragons, the world's largest lizards, live in the wild only in Indonesia.
Most Indonesians live on the island of Borneo.
statements.truth: More than half of Indonesians live on Java, one of the most densely populated islands on Earth.

statements.text: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which runs about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar.
The coffee plant is believed to have come originally from Ethiopia.
Ethiopia has a long coastline on the Red Sea.
statements.truth: Ethiopia has been landlocked since Eritrea became independent in 1993.

statements.text: Mexico City is built on the bed of a former lake, Lake Texcoco.
Mexico officially recognises 68 Indigenous languages.
Mexico's official name is the Republic of Mexico.
statements.truth: Mexico's official name is the United Mexican States (Estados Unidos Mexicanos).

statements.text: Finland has roughly 188,000 lakes.
Finnish isn't related to most European languages. One of its closest relatives is Estonian.
The word 'sauna' was borrowed into Finnish from English.
statements.truth: "Sauna" is a Finnish word, and Finnish sauna culture is on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage.

statements.text: The Great Barrier Reef, off Australia's northeast coast, is the world's largest coral reef system.
Canberra was built as Australia's capital partly as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
Australia has more people than California.
statements.truth: Australia has about 28 million people. California alone has about 39 million.

statements.text: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 1400s.
Lake Titicaca, on Peru's border with Bolivia, is often called the highest navigable lake in the world.
Peru's currency is the peso.
statements.truth: Peru's currency is the sol.

statements.text: Istanbul stretches across two continents, Europe and Asia.
Saint Nicholas, who inspired the legend of Santa Claus, was born in what is now Türkiye.
Istanbul is the capital of Türkiye.
statements.truth: The capital is Ankara. Istanbul is the largest city.

statements.text: In 1893, New Zealand became the first self-governing country to let women vote in national elections.
New Zealand has no native land snakes.
The kiwi, New Zealand's national bird, can fly short distances.
statements.truth: Kiwi are flightless. Their wings are tiny and hidden under their feathers.

statements.text: Mongolia is the most sparsely populated independent country in the world.
The Mongol Empire, founded by Genghis Khan, became the largest connected land empire in history.
Mongolia has a coastline on the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Mongolia is landlocked, sitting between Russia and China.

statements.text: Greece has around 6,000 islands and islets, but only about 227 are inhabited.
The marathon race is named after Marathon, a town in Greece.
The ancient Olympic Games were held in Athens.
statements.truth: The ancient Games were held at Olympia, in the western Peloponnese. Athens hosted the first modern Games in 1896.

statements.text: Vietnam is one of the world's biggest coffee exporters.
Hạ Long Bay is dotted with around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's capital.
statements.truth: The capital is Hanoi, in the north. Ho Chi Minh City is the largest city.

statements.text: South Africa has 12 official languages.
South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.
Table Mountain overlooks Johannesburg.
statements.truth: Table Mountain overlooks Cape Town, more than 1,200 km (750 mi) from Johannesburg.

statements.text: Argentina is the eighth-largest country in the world by area.
Aconcagua, in Argentina, is the highest mountain outside Asia.
The tango was invented in the 1980s for a television dance contest.
statements.truth: The tango grew up in the late 1800s around the Río de la Plata, in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

statements.text: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh.
Bern is officially called Switzerland's "federal city" rather than its capital.
The Matterhorn is Switzerland's highest mountain.
statements.truth: Switzerland's highest peak is the Dufourspitze, at 4,634 m. The Matterhorn is 4,478 m.

statements.text: Sri Lanka's tea is still sold as 'Ceylon tea', after the island's old name.
Sigiriya in Sri Lanka is an ancient rock fortress on top of a rock about 180 m (590 ft) high.
True cinnamon originally comes from South America.
statements.truth: True cinnamon, also called Ceylon cinnamon, is native to Sri Lanka.

statements.text: Vienna's Tiergarten Schönbrunn, opened in 1752, is the oldest zoo still running in the world.
Austria's Eisriesenwelt is the largest ice cave in the world.
Vienna's famous Sachertorte is a lemon sponge cake.
statements.truth: The Sachertorte is a chocolate sponge cake with apricot jam and a chocolate glaze, credited to Vienna's Franz Sacher.

statements.text: Haiti shares the Caribbean island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.
French and Haitian Creole are the two official languages of Haiti.
Haiti is an island nation in the South Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Haiti is in the Caribbean Sea, on the western side of the island of Hispaniola.

statements.text: Togo is an island nation in the Indian Ocean, off the coast of East Africa.
statements.truth: Togo is on the West African mainland, between Ghana and Benin.

statements.text: French is the official language of Togo.
Togo's capital, Lomé, sits on the coast of the Gulf of Guinea.
Zambia's capital city is Lusaka.
Victoria Falls, one of the world's most famous waterfalls, sits on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
Zambia has a long coastline on the Indian Ocean with sandy beaches.
statements.truth: Zambia is a landlocked country in Southern Africa with no coastline.

statements.text: The desert planet Tatooine in the first Star Wars film was filmed in Tunisia.
The ancient city of Carthage stood on the shore of the Lake of Tunis, in what is now Tunisia.
Tunisia's capital, Tunis, was named after the country.
statements.truth: It is the other way round: Tunisia is named after its capital city, Tunis.

statements.text: Sweden's Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi is rebuilt from ice and snow every winter.
Sweden's 'allemansrätten', or everyman's right, lets people hike across and even camp for a night or two on other people's land.
All the Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.
statements.truth: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway.

statements.text: Venezuela's Angel Falls is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall.
Near Venezuela's Lake Maracaibo, the Catatumbo lightning storms flash on 140 to 160 nights a year.
The name Venezuela means 'land of mountains'.
statements.truth: Venezuela means 'Little Venice'. Explorers were reminded of Venice by houses built on stilts over the water.

statements.text: Kazakhstan is the largest landlocked country in the world.
Vostok 1, which carried Yuri Gagarin into space, was launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
The wild ancestor of the apple has never grown in Kazakhstan.
statements.truth: The main wild ancestor of today's apple, Malus sieversii, grows in the mountains of Central Asia, including Kazakhstan.

statements.text: Lesotho has long sandy beaches along the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Lesotho is landlocked and completely surrounded by South Africa.

statements.text: Lesotho is a kingdom, and its capital city is Maseru.
Lesotho is a very mountainous country in southern Africa.
Portuguese is the official language of Angola.
Angola is a country in South America.
statements.truth: Angola is in Southern Africa, across the Atlantic Ocean from Brazil.

statements.text: Angola has a long coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.
The United States bought Alaska from Russia in 1867.
Yellowstone, established in 1872, is considered the first national park in the world.
The Statue of Liberty was designed by an American sculptor.
statements.truth: The Statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and was a gift from France.

statements.text: The shore of the Dead Sea, on Jordan's western border, is the lowest land on Earth.
Petra's famous buildings are carved directly into pinkish sandstone cliffs.
Jordan has no coastline at all.
statements.truth: Jordan has a short coastline on the Gulf of Aqaba, at its port city of Aqaba.

statements.text: The cravat, ancestor of the necktie, became fashionable in France in the 1660s thanks to the knotted neck scarves of Croatian soldiers.
Croatia has more than 1,000 islands and islets along its Adriatic coast.
The Dalmatian dog breed is named after a Croatian king.
statements.truth: The Dalmatian is named after Dalmatia, a region of Croatia on the Adriatic coast.

statements.text: Burkina Faso is a coastal country in East Africa with beaches on the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa.

statements.text: The capital and largest city of Burkina Faso is Ouagadougou.
Burkina Faso shares a border with Ghana to the south.
Spain's national anthem, the Marcha Real, has no official lyrics.
At La Tomatina, a festival in the town of Buñol, people throw tomatoes at each other.
The Sagrada Família in Barcelona was completed in 1926.
statements.truth: Construction began in 1882 and has gone on for well over a century. Gaudí died in 1926 with the church far from finished.

statements.text: Lake Malawi, a huge lake, runs along most of Malawi's eastern border.
Malawi is an island nation in the Caribbean Sea.
statements.truth: Malawi is a landlocked country in southeast Africa.

statements.text: Malawi is nicknamed "the Warm Heart of Africa" for its friendly people.
Colombia's Caño Cristales is nicknamed the 'river of five colours'.
Colombia has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.
Colombia is named after its first president.
statements.truth: Colombia is named after Christopher Columbus.

statements.text: Eswatini is a small kingdom in Southern Africa.
Eswatini is almost completely surrounded by South Africa, with Mozambique on its eastern side.
Eswatini is famous for its long sandy beaches on the Atlantic Ocean.
statements.truth: Eswatini is landlocked, so it has no coastline at all.

statements.text: Oman is located on the Arabian Peninsula in West Asia.
Oman's capital city is Dubai.
statements.truth: Oman's capital is Muscat. Dubai is a city in the United Arab Emirates.

statements.text: Arabic is the official language of Oman.
The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa.
The Gambia is surrounded by Senegal on every side except its Atlantic coast.
Spanish is the official language of The Gambia.
statements.truth: English is the official language of The Gambia.

statements.text: Bengali, also called Bangla, is the official language of Bangladesh.
The Bengal tiger is the national animal of Bangladesh.
Bangladesh shares land borders with five countries.
statements.truth: Bangladesh borders only two countries: India, which surrounds it on almost every side, and Myanmar.

statements.text: Paraguay is a landlocked country in the middle of South America.
Paraguay has two official languages: Spanish and Guaraní.
Paraguay's capital city is Ciudad del Este.
statements.truth: Paraguay's capital is Asunción.

statements.text: Zimbabwe has a long coastline on the Atlantic Ocean.
statements.truth: Zimbabwe is landlocked and has no coastline at all.

statements.text: The famous Victoria Falls waterfall is shared by Zimbabwe and Zambia.
Harare is the capital and largest city of Zimbabwe.
San Marino is a small, flat island in the middle of the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: San Marino is landlocked, perched on Monte Titano and completely surrounded by Italy.

statements.text: San Marino is a tiny country completely surrounded by Italy.
Italian is the official language of San Marino.
A gold harp on a blue background is Ireland's coat of arms.
Newgrange, a passage tomb in Ireland built around 3100 BC, is older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
Halloween grew out of an old Irish festival called Beltane.
statements.truth: Halloween's roots lie in Samhain, a Gaelic festival marking the end of the harvest. Beltane is a spring festival.

statements.text: Liberia is a country in South America.
statements.truth: Liberia is in West Africa, on the Atlantic coast.

statements.text: Liberia's capital and largest city is Monrovia.
English is the official language of Liberia.
Djibouti is a small country in the Horn of Africa.
Djibouti is landlocked, with no access to the sea.
statements.truth: Djibouti has a coastline on the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.

statements.text: French and Arabic are the two official languages of Djibouti.
Armenia's capital city is Yerevan.
Armenia has a long, sunny coastline on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Armenia is a landlocked country in the South Caucasus.

statements.text: The Armenian language is written in its own unique alphabet.
Antigua and Barbuda is an island country in the Caribbean.
Antigua and Barbuda is an island nation in the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Antigua and Barbuda is in the Caribbean.

statements.text: The country is named after its two main islands, Antigua and Barbuda.
The saxophone was invented by Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax.
Belgium has three official languages: Dutch, French and German.
Brussels' famous Manneken Pis statue is more than 10 m (33 ft) tall.
statements.truth: The Manneken Pis is tiny, only about 55.5 cm (22 in) tall.

statements.text: Most people in Honduras speak Portuguese.
statements.truth: Spanish is the official language of Honduras, spoken by almost everyone.

statements.text: Honduras is in Central America and has a coastline on the Caribbean Sea.
The ancient Maya city of Copán is found in Honduras.
São Tomé and Príncipe is an island country in the Gulf of Guinea, off Central Africa.
Portuguese is the official language of São Tomé and Príncipe.
São Tomé and Príncipe is a landlocked country in the middle of the Sahara Desert.
statements.truth: São Tomé and Príncipe is made up of islands in the Gulf of Guinea.

statements.text: Timor-Leste is a country in Southeast Asia that shares the island of Timor with Indonesia.
Timor-Leste's two official languages are Portuguese and Tetum.
Timor-Leste is a landlocked country with no coastline.
statements.truth: Timor-Leste is an island country covering the eastern half of the island of Timor.

statements.text: The DR Congo is named after the mighty Congo River, which flows through it.
Kinshasa is the capital and largest city of the DR Congo.
The DR Congo is a small island nation in the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: The DR Congo is a huge country in Central Africa, the second-largest in Africa.

statements.text: Lake Volta in Ghana is one of the largest artificial lakes in the world by surface area.
On 6 March 1957, Ghana became the first colony in sub-Saharan Africa to gain independence.
Kente cloth is printed by machine and never woven.
statements.truth: Kente is a woven cloth from Ghana, made by the Akan and Ewe peoples.

statements.text: Benin is in East Africa, on the Indian Ocean coast.
statements.truth: Benin is in West Africa, between Togo and Nigeria.

statements.text: French is the official language of Benin.
Benin's neighbours include Togo to the west and Nigeria to the east.
Liechtenstein has sunny beaches along the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: Liechtenstein is a landlocked country in the Alps between Switzerland and Austria.

statements.text: The capital of Liechtenstein is Vaduz.
German is the official language of Liechtenstein.
The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
Most people in the Dominican Republic speak French.
statements.truth: The Dominican Republic is mostly Spanish-speaking.

statements.text: Baseball is by far the most popular sport in the Dominican Republic.
Georgia's capital city is Tbilisi.
Georgia is home to some of the world's earliest known winemaking sites.
The country of Georgia is landlocked, with no sea coast.
statements.truth: Georgia lies on the east coast of the Black Sea.

statements.text: The capital of Seychelles is Victoria.
Seychelles is a group of islands in the Caribbean Sea.
statements.truth: Seychelles is a group of islands in the Indian Ocean, east of Africa.

statements.text: Huge numbers of giant tortoises live on Aldabra, an atoll in Seychelles.
The Lut Desert in Iran has recorded some of the hottest ground temperatures on Earth, up to 70.7 °C (159 °F).
Qanats, underground channels that carry water from hills to farms, were developed in ancient Iran.
Persian, Iran's main language, is a form of Arabic.
statements.truth: Persian is an Indo-European language, though it is written in a script based on Arabic.

statements.text: Belize is an island nation in the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: Belize is in Central America, on the coast of the Caribbean Sea.

statements.text: English is the official language of Belize.
Belize is famous for its huge barrier reef in the Caribbean Sea.
Malta's Ġgantija temples, on the island of Gozo, are older than the pyramids of Egypt.
Maltese grew out of Sicilian Arabic but is written in the Latin alphabet.
Malta is made up of a single island.
statements.truth: Malta is an archipelago. Its three main islands are Malta, Gozo and Comino.

statements.text: Rwanda is a landlocked country in East Africa.
Rwanda is a vast, flat desert country in North Africa.
statements.truth: Rwanda is a small, hilly country in East Africa, nicknamed the land of a thousand hills.

statements.text: Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park is a famous home of mountain gorillas.
Bhutan sits in the Himalayas, between China and India.
Bhutan's capital and largest city is Thimphu.
Ice hockey is Bhutan's national sport.
statements.truth: Archery is the national sport of Bhutan.

statements.text: Botswana is home to the Okavango Delta, a vast inland river delta.
Botswana is a landlocked country in southern Africa.
Botswana's capital city is Francistown.
statements.truth: Gaborone is the capital of Botswana.

statements.text: Saint Lucia is an island country in the eastern Caribbean Sea.
The Pitons, two steep volcanic peaks, are Saint Lucia's most famous landmark.
Saint Lucia is an island country in the Pacific Ocean.
statements.truth: Saint Lucia is in the eastern Caribbean Sea, part of the West Indies.

statements.text: The official language of Mozambique is French.
statements.truth: Portuguese is the official language of Mozambique.

statements.text: Mozambique is in Southeast Africa, with the Indian Ocean along its eastern coast.
Maputo is the capital and largest city of Mozambique.
Skopje is the capital and largest city of North Macedonia.
North Macedonia has a long coastline on the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: North Macedonia is a landlocked country in southeastern Europe, in the Balkans.

statements.text: Lake Ohrid lies on North Macedonia's border with Albania.
Zuma Rock, a huge natural monolith in Nigeria, appears on the 100-naira banknote.
More than 500 native languages are spoken in Nigeria.
Lagos is Nigeria's capital.
statements.truth: Abuja has been Nigeria's capital since 1991. Lagos is its biggest city.

statements.text: The Philippines is made up of more than 7,600 islands.
The Chocolate Hills on Bohol are more than 1,000 grassy, cone-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season.
The Philippines is named after an ancient island goddess.
statements.truth: The Philippines is named after King Philip II of Spain.

statements.text: Uganda has a long coastline on the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Uganda is landlocked, though it shares the huge Lake Victoria with Kenya and Tanzania.

statements.text: Uganda's capital city is Kampala.
English and Swahili are the official languages of Uganda.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an island country in the eastern Caribbean.
The capital of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is on the small island of Bequia.
statements.truth: The capital is Kingstown, on the main island of Saint Vincent.

statements.text: English is the official language of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines.
The Rubik's Cube was invented in 1974 by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik.
Hungary's Lake Hévíz is the largest thermal lake in Europe that people can swim in.
Hungarian is closely related to German.
statements.truth: Hungarian is a Uralic language, distantly related to Finnish and Estonian.

statements.text: Moldova has many sandy beaches on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Moldova is landlocked, sitting between Romania and Ukraine.

statements.text: Moldova is well known for making and exporting wine.
Chișinău is the capital and largest city of Moldova.
Trinidad and Tobago is a Caribbean country just off the coast of Venezuela.
The main official language of Trinidad and Tobago is Portuguese.
statements.truth: English is the official language of Trinidad and Tobago.

statements.text: Trinidad and Tobago is the birthplace of the steelpan, a drum made from steel.
Gabon is on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, and the equator runs through it.
Libreville is the capital and largest city of Gabon.
Spanish is the official language of Gabon.
statements.truth: French is the official language of Gabon.

statements.text: Andorra sits high in the Pyrenees mountains, between France and Spain.
Catalan is the official language of Andorra.
Andorra is one of the biggest countries in Europe.
statements.truth: Andorra is a tiny microstate, one of the smallest countries in Europe.

statements.text: Qatar's only land border is with Saudi Arabia.
Khor Al Adaid in Qatar is an 'inland sea' where the Persian Gulf reaches deep into the desert.
Qatar is an island in the Persian Gulf.
statements.truth: Qatar is a peninsula that juts out from the Arabian Peninsula into the Persian Gulf.

statements.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is made up of two islands in the Caribbean.
English is the official language of Saint Kitts and Nevis.
Saint Kitts and Nevis is one of the biggest countries in the Americas.
statements.truth: Saint Kitts and Nevis is the smallest sovereign country in the Western Hemisphere.

statements.text: English is the official language of the Republic of the Congo.
statements.truth: French is the official language of the Republic of the Congo.

statements.text: The capital and largest city of the Republic of the Congo is Brazzaville.
The Republic of the Congo is in Central Africa and lies on the equator.
Slovakia is a landlocked country in Central Europe.
Prague is the capital of Slovakia.
statements.truth: Bratislava is the capital of Slovakia; Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic.

statements.text: The Tatra Mountains rise in the north of Slovakia.
The capital of Laos is Vientiane.
Laos has long sandy beaches along the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.

statements.text: Sticky rice is a staple food in Laos.
Marie Curie, the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, was born in Warsaw.
Poland's Wieliczka Salt Mine has underground chapels and statues carved by miners out of rock salt.
Poland's Białowieża Forest is home to Europe's last wild tigers.
statements.truth: Białowieża Forest is famous for its European bison, Europe's heaviest land animal.

statements.text: Bulgaria is a country in Southeastern Europe, on the Balkan Peninsula.
Bulgaria's capital city is Plovdiv.
statements.truth: Bulgaria's capital is Sofia.

statements.text: Bulgaria has a coastline on the Black Sea.
Romania's Palace of the Parliament in Bucharest is described as the world's heaviest administrative building.
Romanian is a Romance language, descended from Latin.
The Danube Delta lies in Romania's mountainous north.
statements.truth: The Danube Delta lies where the Danube meets the Black Sea, mostly in Romania, with a small part in Ukraine.

statements.text: Ecuador's name is simply the Spanish word for 'equator'.
Because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo is the farthest point from Earth's centre.
Ecuador's famous toquilla straw hats are woven from sheep's wool.
statements.truth: They're woven by hand from the leaves of the toquilla palm. They're better known abroad as Panama hats.

statements.text: Mauritius is a landlocked country in central Africa.
statements.truth: Mauritius is an island country in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar.

statements.text: The dodo, a famous flightless bird, once lived only on Mauritius.
Port Louis is the capital and largest city of Mauritius.
Singapore is made up of one main island and more than 60 smaller islands and islets.
The name Singapore goes back to a Sanskrit word meaning 'Lion City'.
Singapore lies more than 1,000 km (620 mi) north of the equator.
statements.truth: Singapore is only about 137 km (85 mi) north of the equator.

statements.text: Big Ben is the nickname of the great bell in London's clock tower, not the tower itself.
The London Underground began in 1863 with the world's first underground passenger railway.
Stonehenge was built by the Romans.
statements.truth: Stonehenge was built in prehistoric times, roughly 3000 to 2000 BC, thousands of years before the Romans arrived.

statements.text: Most people in Uzbekistan speak Hindi as their main language.
statements.truth: Uzbek, a Turkic language, is the official language of Uzbekistan.

statements.text: Uzbekistan is a country in Central Asia.
The Registan, a grand square lined with three madrasas, is a famous landmark in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
Mali is a country in West Africa.
The historic city of Timbuktu, once a famous centre of learning, is in Mali.
Mali is a chain of tropical islands in the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Mali is a landlocked country in West Africa. The island nation is the Maldives.

statements.text: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world by area.
The Pontifical Swiss Guard has protected the popes since 1506.
Vatican City has its own airport.
statements.truth: Vatican City has no airport, though it does have a heliport and a short railway.

statements.text: Nicaragua is the largest country in Central America by area.

Savai'i, Samoa's largest island, is known for its blowholes and waterfalls.
Romania's Bran Castle is famous as 'Dracula's Castle'.
Romania's Transfăgărășan mountain road was called 'the best road in the world' on Top Gear.
Romania's capital is Budapest.
statements.truth: Bucharest is Romania's capital. Budapest is the capital of Hungary.

statements.text: Classic 1950s American cars are still everyday cars and taxis on Cuba's roads.
The cha-cha-chá was created in the 1990s by a pop band.
statements.truth: The cha-cha-chá comes from Cuba, where violinist Enrique Jorrín created it in the early 1950s.

statements.text: The daiquiri cocktail is named after a beach near Santiago de Cuba.
Gabon's Oklo is the only place on Earth where natural nuclear reactors are known to have existed.
Gabon's forest elephants are bigger than Africa's savanna elephants.
statements.truth: Forest elephants are considerably smaller than savanna (bush) elephants.

statements.text: Around 95,000 forest elephants live in Gabon's rainforests.
Thailand's national animal is the tiger.
statements.truth: Thailand's national animal is the Thai elephant, which has been a symbol of the country for centuries.

statements.text: Thailand's Kitti's hog-nosed bat, or bumblebee bat, is one of the smallest mammals in the world.
Thailand celebrates its traditional New Year, Songkran, with giant water fights.
The 180th meridian, opposite Greenwich, runs across Fiji's island of Taveuni.
Fiji Water is bottled from an underground aquifer in Fiji.
Fiji's traditional drink, kava, is made from coconuts.
statements.truth: Kava is made from the ground-up roots of the kava plant, a type of pepper plant.

statements.text: Mali has a long Atlantic coastline.
statements.truth: Mali is landlocked, in the middle of West Africa.

statements.text: Mansa Musa, a ruler of the medieval Mali Empire, is often called one of the richest people in history.
Mali's Dogon people built villages along the steep Bandiagara cliffs.
The Netherlands has about 18 million bicycles, more than one for every Dutch person old enough to ride.
The Netherlands is the world's second-largest exporter of food and farm products.
Holland is the official name of the whole country.
statements.truth: Holland is just one region, made up of two of the country's twelve provinces. The country's name is the Netherlands.

statements.text: Selling chewing gum is largely banned in Singapore.
English is Singapore's only official language.
statements.truth: Singapore has four official languages: English, Malay, Mandarin Chinese and Tamil.

statements.text: Singapore's Changi Airport has the tallest indoor waterfall in the world.
Dominica is the youngest island in the Lesser Antilles and is still being shaped by volcanoes.
Spanish is the official language of Dominica.
statements.truth: English is Dominica's official language, and many people also speak a French-based creole.

statements.text: Sperm whales can be seen off Dominica all year round.
Vietnam is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Vietnam has a long coastline on the South China Sea and the Gulf of Thailand.

statements.text: Vietnam's Sơn Đoòng is the largest known cave passage in the world.
Vietnamese is written in the Latin alphabet, with lots of extra accent marks.
The flamingo is the national bird of the Bahamas.
Christopher Columbus's first landfall in the Americas in 1492 was in the Bahamas.
The Bahamas uses the euro.
statements.truth: The Bahamas uses the Bahamian dollar, which is worth the same as one US dollar.

statements.text: São Tomé and Príncipe has a cold, snowy climate.
statements.truth: The islands sit near the equator and have a hot, humid tropical climate.

statements.text: The islands of São Tomé and Príncipe were formed by volcanoes about 30 million years ago.
Pico Cão Grande in São Tomé is a needle-shaped volcanic tower rising high above the jungle.
Switzerland's flag is square, one of only two square national flags.
Switzerland has enough fallout shelter places for more than its entire population.
Switzerland uses the euro.
statements.truth: Switzerland is not in the EU and uses its own currency, the Swiss franc.

statements.text: The Solomon Islands are made up of six major islands and more than 1,000 smaller ones.
The Solomon Islands are mostly covered by sandy desert.
statements.truth: The Solomon Islands are mostly rugged, forested volcanic islands with a hot, wet climate.

statements.text: Shell money is still used for traditional payments in parts of the Solomon Islands.
Canada Post gives Santa Claus his own postal code: H0H 0H0.
Most of the world's maple syrup comes from British Columbia.
statements.truth: Quebec, on the other side of Canada, produces most of the world's maple syrup.

statements.text: Canada and the United States share the longest international border in the world.
Brunei covers most of the island of Borneo.
statements.truth: Brunei is a small country on Borneo's northern coast. Most of Borneo belongs to Indonesia and Malaysia.

statements.text: The Sultan of Brunei's Istana Nurul Iman is the world's largest residential palace.
Brunei has one of the highest rates of car ownership in the world.
The Galápagos Islands, famous for giant tortoises, belong to Ecuador.
Ecuador uses the US dollar as its currency.
Ecuador's capital, Quito, sits right at sea level.
statements.truth: Quito is high in the Andes, about 2,850 m (9,350 ft) up, one of the highest capitals in the world.

statements.text: Lagos is the capital of Angola.
statements.truth: Luanda is Angola's capital. Lagos is a huge city in Nigeria.

statements.text: Angola is the second-largest Portuguese-speaking country in the world, after Brazil.
Angola is about twice the size of France.
Monaco has the highest population density of any country.
Monaco has no personal income tax, except for French citizens living there.
Monaco shares land borders with three countries.
statements.truth: Monaco's only land neighbour is France. Italy is just a few kilometres further along the coast.

statements.text: Tajikistan's Pamir Highway is one of the highest main roads in the world.
Tajikistan's capital city is Khujand.
statements.truth: Dushanbe is Tajikistan's capital.

statements.text: Tajikistan's Nurek Dam is one of the tallest dams in the world.
Paraguay's flag has a different emblem on its front and back.
Paraguay's ñandutí lace is woven from real spider silk.
statements.truth: Ñandutí is a traditional lace stitched on a frame. Its Guaraní name just means 'spider web'.

statements.text: Paraguay's capital, Asunción, sits on the banks of the Paraguay River.
Several species of wild snake live in the Irish countryside.
statements.truth: Ireland has no native snakes. They most likely never arrived after the last Ice Age.

statements.text: Guinness stout was first brewed in Dublin in 1759.
Bram Stoker, who wrote Dracula, was born in Dublin.
Mauritania's Banc d'Arguin National Park is a major stop for migrating birds such as flamingos and pelicans.
Chinguetti in Mauritania has ancient family libraries full of old manuscripts.
Mauritania's Banc d'Arguin National Park lies deep inland, far from the sea.
statements.truth: Banc d'Arguin is on Mauritania's Atlantic coast, between Nouakchott and Nouadhibou.

statements.text: Auckland is the capital of New Zealand.
statements.truth: Wellington is New Zealand's capital. Auckland is the biggest city.

statements.text: A hill in New Zealand has one of the longest place names in the world, with 85 letters.
The Lord of the Rings films were shot in New Zealand.
Colombia produces more emeralds than any other country.
Colombia has more bird species than any other country in the world.
Colombia's capital is Medellín.
statements.truth: Bogotá, high in the Andes, is Colombia's capital. Medellín is its second-largest city.

statements.text: Larimar, a sky-blue gemstone, is found only in the Dominican Republic.
The Dominican Republic and Dominica are the same country.
statements.truth: They're different countries. Dominica is a small island nation far to the southeast, in the Lesser Antilles.

statements.text: The Dominican Republic's salty Lake Enriquillo lies below sea level and is home to lots of crocodiles.
Mozart was born in Salzburg, Austria, in 1756.
Austria has a coastline on the Adriatic Sea.
statements.truth: Austria is landlocked, surrounded by eight countries in the middle of Europe.

statements.text: China built a full-size copy of the Austrian lakeside village of Hallstatt.
Oman is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Oman has a long coastline on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman.

statements.text: Oman's mountain Jebel Shams is home to a canyon nicknamed the 'Grand Canyon of Arabia'.
Oman's Bimmah Sinkhole is a turquoise pool only about 600 m (2,000 ft) from the sea.
Ganvié, a village built in a lake in Benin, is nicknamed the 'Venice of Africa'.
Benin's official capital is Porto-Novo, but the government mostly works from Cotonou.
Benin has no coastline.
statements.truth: Benin has a short coastline on the Bight of Benin, part of the Atlantic Ocean.

statements.text: Kiribati uses the euro.
statements.truth: Kiribati uses the Australian dollar.

statements.text: Kiribati's Kiritimati is one of the first places on Earth to welcome each New Year.
Kiribati's Phoenix Islands Protected Area is one of the largest marine reserves in the world.
Lithuania's Curonian Spit has some of the highest moving sand dunes in Europe.
A French scientist worked out that the geographical centre of Europe lies in Lithuania, near Vilnius.
Lithuanian is a Slavic language closely related to Russian.
statements.truth: Lithuanian is a Baltic language. Its closest living relative is Latvian.

statements.text: The world's first human heart transplant was performed in Cape Town in 1967.
No penguins live in the wild in South Africa.
statements.truth: African penguins live along South Africa's coast, and a colony at Boulders Beach near Cape Town is a famous sight.

statements.text: South Africa mines more platinum than any other country.
Khone Phapheng Falls in Laos is the largest waterfall in Southeast Asia.
Laos has never had a currency of its own.
statements.truth: Laos has its own currency, the kip, used since 1953.

statements.text: Laos' Si Phan Don area on the Mekong is nicknamed the 'Four Thousand Islands'.
Venezuela is in Central America.
statements.truth: Venezuela is on the northern coast of South America.

statements.text: Venezuela has the largest known oil reserves in the world.
Venezuela's Mérida cable car is the highest in the world, climbing to about 4,765 m (15,633 ft).
Seychelles has the smallest population of any African country.
Seychelles sits on a sunken slab of granite, a tiny 'microcontinent' once wedged between Madagascar and India.
Spanish is one of Seychelles' official languages.
statements.truth: Seychelles' official languages are Seychellois Creole, English and French.

statements.text: Uzbekistan's national dish, plov, is a noodle soup.
statements.truth: Plov is a hearty rice dish cooked with meat, carrots and onions.

statements.text: Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world.
Samarkand, in Uzbekistan, was one of the great cities of the Silk Road.
Guatemala's Semuc Champey is a natural limestone bridge with a river rushing underneath it.
Tiny 'worry dolls' are a traditional craft from Guatemala.
Antigua is the capital of Guatemala.
statements.truth: Guatemala City is the capital. Antigua Guatemala was the old colonial capital.

statements.text: Slovakia makes more cars per person than any other country.
Slovakia still uses the koruna, its own currency.
statements.truth: Slovakia replaced the koruna with the euro in 2009.

statements.text: Slovakia's Dobšiná Ice Cave, filled with frozen ice formations, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
La Paz and El Alto have the longest urban cable car network in the world.
Bolivia is named after a famous river.
statements.truth: Bolivia is named after Simón Bolívar, a leader of South America's fight for independence from Spain.

statements.text: Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni holds a huge share of the world's lithium.
Namibia's Skeleton Coast faces the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: The Skeleton Coast is on Namibia's Atlantic shore, on the west side of Africa.

statements.text: Namibia's Fish River Canyon is the largest canyon in Africa.
Namibia's Sossusvlei is surrounded by giant red sand dunes.
Argentina's Ushuaia is often called the southernmost city in the world.
Football superstar Lionel Messi was born in the Argentine city of Rosario.
Argentina's capital, Buenos Aires, lies on the Pacific coast.
statements.truth: Buenos Aires sits on the Río de la Plata, on the Atlantic side of South America. The Andes separate Argentina from the Pacific.

statements.text: Kuwait is one of the largest countries in Asia.
statements.truth: Kuwait is a small country, wedged between Iraq to the north and Saudi Arabia to the south.

statements.text: Kuwait Towers, three slim towers topped with spheres, are a famous landmark on Kuwait City's coast.
Ancient Greeks under Alexander the Great named Kuwait's Failaka Island 'Ikaros'.
Norway's Lærdal Tunnel is the longest road tunnel in the world, at about 24.5 km (15 mi).
Every year the city of Oslo gives London a giant Christmas tree for Trafalgar Square.
Norway's capital is Stockholm.
statements.truth: Oslo is Norway's capital. Stockholm is the capital of neighbouring Sweden.

statements.text: Alaska has a longer coastline than all the other US states combined.
Washington, D.C. lies inside Washington State.
statements.truth: Washington, D.C. is on the East Coast, between Maryland and Virginia. Washington State is on the opposite side of the country.

statements.text: Measured from its base deep under the ocean, Hawaii's Mauna Kea is taller than Mount Everest.
Kenya's M-Pesa was a pioneer of sending money by mobile phone.
Kenya's official languages are English and French.
statements.truth: Kenya's official languages are English and Swahili.

statements.text: Huge herds of wildebeest cross Kenya's Maasai Mara each year in the Great Migration.
Costa Rica has no volcanoes.
statements.truth: Costa Rica has several volcanoes, including Arenal, one of its most famous and once very active.

statements.text: Hundreds of ancient, almost perfectly round stone spheres have been found in Costa Rica.
Costa Rica is home to about 5% of all the world's plant and animal species.
Chimpanzees in Côte d'Ivoire's Taï National Park are famous for using tools.
Football legend Didier Drogba is from Côte d'Ivoire.
Attiéké, a favourite food in Côte d'Ivoire, is made from rice.
statements.truth: Attiéké is made from grated, fermented cassava, and looks a bit like couscous.

statements.text: Azerbaijani is closely related to Japanese.
statements.truth: Azerbaijani is a Turkic language, closely related to Turkish.

statements.text: Azerbaijan and its Caspian coast are home to nearly 400 mud volcanoes.
Baku is the lowest-lying national capital in the world, below sea level.
Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean Sea.
A cat buried with a person about 9,500 years ago in Cyprus is one of the earliest signs of pet cats.
Cars in Cyprus drive on the right-hand side of the road.
statements.truth: Cyprus drives on the left, a habit left over from British rule.

statements.text: Djibouti's Lake Abbé is dotted with limestone chimneys up to 50 m (160 ft) tall that puff out steam.
Djibouti's Lake Assal is a freshwater lake.
statements.truth: Lake Assal is a very salty lake, lying 155 m (509 ft) below sea level.

statements.text: Young whale sharks gather near the shore in Djibouti's Gulf of Tadjoura.
Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, has as many as 400,000 rickshaw drivers.
Kolkata is the capital of Bangladesh.
statements.truth: Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh. Kolkata is a city in India's state of West Bengal.

statements.text: Bangladesh has about 700 rivers.
Albania's name for itself, Shqipëria, is often explained as 'land of the lions'.
statements.truth: Shqipëria is popularly explained as 'land of the eagles', which is why an eagle is on the flag.

statements.text: The ruins of Butrint in Albania were once an ancient Greek city and later a Roman one.
Albanian forms its own branch of the Indo-European languages, with no close living relatives.
The famous 3.2-million-year-old fossil skeleton 'Lucy' was found in Ethiopia.
Ethiopia's Danakil Depression is one of the hottest places on Earth.
Injera, Ethiopia's everyday bread, is a crunchy cracker.
statements.truth: Injera is a soft, spongy, slightly sour flatbread, usually made from a tiny grain called teff.

statements.text: Most Mongolian nomads traditionally lived in igloos.
statements.truth: Mongolian nomads live in a ger, also called a yurt: a round tent of felt over a wooden frame.

statements.text: The first dinosaur eggs recognised by scientists were found in Mongolia's Gobi Desert in the 1920s.
Mongolia's horses outnumber its people.
Banjul, the capital of The Gambia, is on an island.
The Gambia River flows right through the middle of The Gambia.
The Gambia is a large desert country.
statements.truth: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa, a thin strip of land along the Gambia River.

statements.text: Malta's Popeye Village was built as a film set for the 1980 Popeye movie.
Malta is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Malta lies south of Sicily, about 80 km (50 mi) from Italy, in the middle of the Mediterranean.

statements.text: English and Maltese are both official languages of Malta.
The gemstone tanzanite is found in only one place on Earth: Tanzania.
Tanzania is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Tanzania has a long coastline on the Indian Ocean, including the islands of Zanzibar.

statements.text: Queen singer Freddie Mercury was born in Zanzibar, now part of Tanzania.
Doubles, a famous Trinidad street food, is a sweet dessert.
statements.truth: Doubles is a savoury snack of curried chickpeas wrapped in two pieces of fried flatbread.

statements.text: The scarlet ibis is one of Trinidad and Tobago's national birds.
Tobago's Main Ridge Forest Reserve was protected in 1776, one of the oldest such reserves in the world.
Basketball is the most popular sport in the Philippines.
An adult Philippine tarsier, one of the smallest primates, is only about the size of a human fist.
The Philippines' official languages are Spanish and English.
statements.truth: The official languages are Filipino and English. Spanish was official in the past but isn't any more.

statements.text: Nigeria is named after the Congo River.
statements.truth: Nigeria, like its neighbour Niger, is named after the Niger River.

statements.text: Nigeria has the largest population of any country in Africa.
Nigeria's film industry, Nollywood, is one of the biggest in the world by number of films made.
The Rosetta Stone, which helped decode hieroglyphs, was found in Egypt in 1799.
Egypt stretches across two continents, as its Sinai Peninsula is in Asia.
The Sphinx at Giza has the body of a human and the head of a lion.
statements.truth: It's the other way round: the Great Sphinx has the body of a lion and the head of a human.

statements.text: The giant Amazon water lily, with floating leaves up to 3 m (10 ft) across, grows in Guyana.
Guyana's capital city is Linden.
statements.truth: Georgetown is Guyana's capital.

statements.text: Most of Guyana's people live along its narrow Atlantic coast.
Nishiyama Onsen Keiunkan, a hot spring inn in Japan, is said to be the oldest hotel in the world.
Sushi always contains raw fish.
statements.truth: Sushi is defined by its vinegared rice. Lots of sushi has no raw fish, using cooked seafood, egg or vegetables instead.

statements.text: Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains began running in 1964.
Mostar's famous Old Bridge, Stari Most, is made of wood.
statements.truth: Stari Most is a stone arch bridge, first built by the Ottomans in the 1500s and rebuilt in 2004.

statements.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina reaches the sea at just one town, Neum, on the Adriatic.
Sarajevo's tram line, opened in 1885, was used as a test line for the trams of Vienna.
Budapest was formed in 1873 by joining the cities of Buda, Óbuda and Pest.
Budapest's Line 1 is the oldest electric underground railway in continental Europe.
Paprika is rarely used in Hungarian cooking.
statements.truth: Paprika is a star of Hungarian cooking, giving dishes like goulash their colour and flavour.

statements.text: Cape Verde is a single large island.
statements.truth: Cape Verde is made up of ten volcanic islands in the Atlantic Ocean.

statements.text: Cape Verde's island of Sal, Portuguese for 'salt', is named after its salt ponds.
Cachupa, a slow-cooked stew of corn and beans, is Cape Verde's national dish.
Slovenia's Lake Bled has a tiny island in the middle, topped by a church.
The famous white Lipizzaner horses get their name from Lipica, a village in Slovenia.
Slovenia is one of the largest countries in Europe.
statements.truth: Slovenia is one of Europe's smaller countries, about 20,000 km² (7,800 sq mi).

statements.text: Saint Lucia has produced two Nobel Prize winners, more per person than almost any country.
Saint Lucia uses the euro.
statements.truth: Saint Lucia uses the Eastern Caribbean dollar, shared with several neighbouring islands.

statements.text: Saint Lucia's Sulphur Springs is a bubbling geothermal area inside the crater of an old volcano.
In 1960 Sri Lanka elected the world's first woman prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike.
Sri Lanka is an island off the coast of East Africa.
statements.truth: Sri Lanka lies just off the southern tip of India, in the Indian Ocean.

statements.text: Sri Lanka's Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage cares for dozens of rescued elephants.
The Maldives' official language is Hindi.
statements.truth: The Maldives' official language is Dhivehi, which is related to Sinhala, spoken in Sri Lanka.

statements.text: Malé, the capital of the Maldives, is one of the most densely packed cities in the world.
The Maldives has one of the world's biggest seaplane fleets, flying visitors to island resorts.
Tuvalu's international airport sits just 3 m (9 ft) above sea level.
Tuvalu used to be called the Ellice Islands.
Tuvalu is known for its high, snowy mountains.
statements.truth: Tuvalu is made of low coral islands and atolls, with no hills at all.

statements.text: Tunisia is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Tunisia has a long Mediterranean coastline with popular beaches.

statements.text: Tunisia's amphitheatre at El Jem is one of the best-preserved Roman amphitheatres in the world.
Tunisia is the northernmost country in Africa.
Eritrea's capital, Asmara, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site thanks to its 1930s modernist buildings.
Asmara's Fiat Tagliero building is a petrol station shaped like an aeroplane.
Eritrea is a landlocked country.
statements.truth: Eritrea has a long coastline on the Red Sea, including the Dahlak islands.

statements.text: Venice is built on more than 100 small islands in a lagoon.
Mount Etna in Sicily is an extinct volcano.
statements.truth: Mount Etna is one of the most active volcanoes in the world and erupts often.

statements.text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to tilt while it was still being built.
Cars in Suriname drive on the left-hand side of the road.
Georgetown is the capital of Suriname.
statements.truth: Paramaribo is Suriname's capital. Georgetown is the capital of neighbouring Guyana.

statements.text: Paramaribo's Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral is the largest wooden building in the Western Hemisphere.
Estonia still uses its own currency, the kroon.
statements.truth: Estonia swapped the kroon for the euro in 2011.

statements.text: Kiiking, swinging all the way round a giant swing, is a sport invented in Estonia.
About half of Estonia is covered in forest.
Liberia was the first African republic to gain independence.
More ships are registered in Liberia than in any other country.
Liberia uses the euro.
statements.truth: Liberia uses the Liberian dollar, and US dollars are widely used too.

statements.text: Spain is an island country.
statements.truth: Spain's land neighbours include France, Portugal and Andorra. Italy is across the Mediterranean.

statements.text: Madrid's Botín, opened in 1725, is listed by Guinness as the world's oldest restaurant.
The Canary Islands are probably named after dogs, not canary birds.
Jordan's Wadi Rum desert stood in for Mars in the film The Martian.
The Dead Sea, on Jordan's border, is so salty that people float easily on it.
Petra is the capital of Jordan.
statements.truth: Amman is Jordan's capital. Petra is an ancient city carved into rock in the south.

statements.text: IKEA was founded in Sweden in 1943.
The pop group ABBA formed in the 1990s.
statements.truth: ABBA formed in Stockholm, Sweden, and won Eurovision for Sweden in 1974 with 'Waterloo'.

statements.text: Sweden has more islands than any other country, over 260,000 of them.
Visitors to Palau sign the 'Palau Pledge', promising to protect its nature.
Palau's main language is French.
statements.truth: Palau's official languages are Palauan and English.

statements.text: Huge stone discs used as money on Yap were carved from rock quarried in Palau.
Most of Botswana is covered by thick rainforest.
statements.truth: Much of Botswana is covered by the Kalahari, a dry, sandy savanna.

statements.text: Botswana's Jwaneng mine is said to be the richest diamond mine in the world by value.
Botswana's Chobe National Park has one of the biggest gatherings of elephants in Africa.
UK postage stamps don't show the country's name, just the monarch's head.
Scotland's Loch Ness holds more fresh water than all the lakes of England and Wales combined.
Wales is represented on the Union Jack by its red dragon.
statements.truth: Wales does not appear on the Union Jack at all. The flag combines the crosses of England, Scotland and Ireland.

statements.text: Pakistan has no coastline.
statements.truth: Pakistan has a coastline about 1,000 km (650 mi) long on the Arabian Sea.

statements.text: Pakistan's colourful painted trucks are known around the world as 'truck art'.
Pakistan's Karakoram Highway is one of the highest paved roads in the world.
Brussels' giant Atomium was built for the 1958 World's Fair.
The comic hero Tintin was created by Belgian artist Hergé.
Belgium has no coastline.
statements.truth: Belgium has a short coastline on the North Sea, about 66 km (41 mi) long, lined with seaside towns.

statements.text: Zimbabwe once printed a 100 trillion dollar banknote.
Zimbabwe's capital has been called Harare ever since it was founded.
statements.truth: The city was founded in 1890 as Fort Salisbury, and later renamed Harare.

statements.text: Ancient rock paintings fill the caves of Zimbabwe's Matobo Hills.
Chefchaouen in Morocco is famous for its blue-painted streets.
A Moroccan tagine is a type of flatbread.
statements.truth: A tagine is a slow-cooked stew, named after the clay pot with a cone-shaped lid it's cooked in.

statements.text: Goats in Morocco climb argan trees to eat the fruit.
Grenada's main language is French.
statements.truth: English is Grenada's official language.

statements.text: Grenada's capital, St. George's, is built around a horseshoe-shaped harbour.
Grenada is made up of the main island plus Carriacou and Petite Martinique.
Turkmenistan's capital, Ashgabat, holds a world record for its number of white marble buildings.
Turkmenistan's flag shows five traditional carpet patterns, honouring its famous rug-making.
Turkmenistan has a coastline on the Black Sea.
statements.truth: Turkmenistan's coast is on the Caspian Sea, the world's largest inland body of water.

statements.text: Fairy tale writer Hans Christian Andersen was born in Copenhagen.
statements.truth: Hans Christian Andersen was Danish, born in the city of Odense in 1805.

statements.text: Denmark is home to Bakken, the oldest amusement park still running in the world.
In Denmark, Danish pastries are called 'wienerbrød', meaning Viennese bread.
Mozambique's Bazaruto Archipelago is one of the last places in East Africa where dugongs live.
Mozambique's capital, Maputo, lies near the country's southern tip.
Maputo has had the same name ever since it was founded.
statements.truth: Maputo was called Lourenço Marques until 1976.

statements.text: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other nation.
The Czech Republic has a coastline on the Baltic Sea.
statements.truth: The Czech Republic is landlocked, in the middle of Central Europe.

statements.text: Prague Castle is one of the largest castle complexes in the world.
Most of Madagascar's plants and animals are found nowhere else on Earth.
Madagascar's fossa, the island's top predator, is a type of large bird.
statements.truth: The fossa is a sleek, cat-like mammal, related to mongooses, that hunts lemurs in the forests.

statements.text: Madagascar and Indonesia together grow about two-thirds of the world's vanilla.
Yerevan, Armenia's capital, is one of the newest cities in the world.
statements.truth: Yerevan is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, dating back to a fortress built in 782 BC.

statements.text: Armenia's Wings of Tatev is one of the longest cable cars in the world.
Armenia's Areni-1 cave held the earliest known winery in the world, about 6,100 years old.
Mauritius' 1847 'Post Office' stamps are among the rarest and most valuable stamps in the world.
From the air, sand off Mauritius' Le Morne creates the illusion of an 'underwater waterfall'.
Mauritius lies in the Atlantic Ocean, off West Africa.
statements.truth: Mauritius is in the Indian Ocean, about 2,000 km (1,200 mi) off the southeast coast of Africa, east of Madagascar.

statements.text: Kazakhstan shares a border with only one country.
statements.truth: Kazakhstan borders Russia, China, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. India is much further south.

statements.text: Kazakhstan produces more uranium than any other country.
Almaty was Kazakhstan's capital until 1997, and it is still the country's biggest city.
Around 85% of Malawi's people live in the countryside.
Colourful cichlid fish from Lake Malawi are popular in home aquariums.
Malawi has a coastline on the Indian Ocean.
statements.truth: Malawi is landlocked, though its huge lake can feel like a sea.

statements.text: In 2007 a lost Swiss army unit accidentally marched into Liechtenstein, then quietly turned back.
Liechtenstein is a republic with no royal family.
statements.truth: Liechtenstein is a principality, ruled by a prince from the House of Liechtenstein.

statements.text: Liechtenstein's national anthem uses the same tune as Britain's 'God Save the King'.
The board game snakes and ladders comes from ancient India.
The Taj Mahal was built as a royal palace for an emperor to live in.
statements.truth: The Taj Mahal is a mausoleum. Emperor Shah Jahan built it as a tomb for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

statements.text: The English word 'shampoo' comes from Hindi.
French is the official language of Guinea-Bissau.
statements.truth: Portuguese is Guinea-Bissau's official language, and Guinea-Bissau Creole is widely spoken.

statements.text: Guinea-Bissau's Bijagós Islands, a group of about 88 islands, are a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
Cashew nuts are one of Guinea-Bissau's main exports.
Bhutan absorbs more carbon dioxide than it gives off, making it carbon negative.
Bhutan's Paro Airport is so tricky to fly into that only a few pilots are allowed to land there.
Bhutan's national dish, ema datshi, is a sweet rice pudding.
statements.truth: Ema datshi is a spicy stew of chilli peppers cooked in cheese.

statements.text: Croatian is mostly written in the Cyrillic alphabet.
statements.truth: Croatian is written in the Latin alphabet, with a few extra letters such as č, š and ž.

statements.text: Dubrovnik's old town was used to film King's Landing in Game of Thrones.
Croatia's Plitvice Lakes are a chain of 16 lakes linked by waterfalls.
Uganda's snowy Rwenzori range is nicknamed the 'Mountains of the Moon'.
At Uganda's Murchison Falls, the Nile squeezes through a gap only about 7 m (23 ft) wide.
Uganda is in West Africa, on the Atlantic coast.
statements.truth: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa, on the shores of Lake Victoria.

statements.text: Tonga's Ha'amonga 'a Maui is a huge stone gateway, sometimes called the 'Stonehenge of the Pacific'.
Tonga uses the US dollar.
statements.truth: Tonga uses its own currency, the paʻanga.

statements.text: People first settled Tonga about 2,500 years ago.
Malaysia is split into two main parts by the South China Sea.
Malaysia's currency is the dollar.
statements.truth: Malaysia's currency is the ringgit.

statements.text: Wild orangutans live only on Borneo and Sumatra, including Malaysia's states of Sabah and Sarawak.
Busan is the capital of South Korea.
statements.truth: Seoul is South Korea's capital and largest city. Busan is its second-largest city and biggest port.

statements.text: The martial art taekwondo comes from Korea.
Until 2023, many South Koreans counted themselves a year old at birth, all getting a year older on New Year's Day.
Algeria's Roman ruins at Timgad are nicknamed the 'Pompeii of North Africa'.
Algiers is nicknamed 'the white' for its whitewashed buildings.
Spanish is the main language of Algeria.
statements.truth: Arabic and Tamazight (Berber) are Algeria's official languages, and French is widely used too.

statements.text: Mont Saint-Michel is a mountain peak in the French Alps.
statements.truth: Mont-Saint-Michel is a rocky tidal island off the coast of Normandy, cut off by the sea at high tide.

statements.text: France is the most visited country in the world.
The Louvre in Paris is the most-visited museum in the world.
The ruins of Caracol, an ancient Maya city in Belize, cover a bigger area than modern Belize City.
Belize's national animal is Baird's tapir.
Belize City is the capital of Belize.
statements.truth: Belmopan has been the capital since 1970. Belize City is the biggest city.

statements.text: The 2022 men's FIFA World Cup in Qatar was the first ever held in the Middle East.
Most of Qatar is covered by thick green forest.
statements.truth: Most of Qatar is flat, low-lying desert, with sunshine all year round.

statements.text: More than 80% of Qatar's people live in its capital, Doha.
Gummy bears were invented in Germany, by Haribo founder Hans Riegel.
Germany has a coastline on the Mediterranean Sea.
statements.truth: Germany's coasts are on the North Sea and the Baltic Sea. It doesn't reach the Mediterranean.

statements.text: Munich's Oktoberfest begins in September, not October.
Bahrain is the largest country in the Middle East.
statements.truth: Bahrain is one of the smallest countries in the world, about 760 km² (290 sq mi).

statements.text: In 2004 Bahrain hosted the first Formula One race in the Middle East.
Bahrain's Pearling Path, honouring its long history of pearl diving, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The mobile game Angry Birds was created in Finland.
Finland hosts the World Wife-Carrying Championships.
Wild penguins live in Finnish Lapland.
statements.truth: Wild penguins live almost entirely in the Southern Hemisphere. Lapland is famous for reindeer instead.

statements.text: Spanish is the main language of the Comoros.
statements.truth: The Comoros' official languages are Comorian, Arabic and French.

statements.text: The Comoros produces most of the world's ylang-ylang, a flower oil used in perfume.
The Comoros' farming relies on exporting spices such as vanilla, cinnamon and cloves.
Togo is one of the narrowest countries in the world, less than 115 km (70 mi) wide.
Lake Togo is a lagoon cut off from the Atlantic by a narrow strip of land.
Togo's name means 'land of mountains'.
statements.truth: Togo's name comes from Ewe words meaning 'by the water' or 'behind the sea'.

statements.text: Russia stretches across 11 time zones.
Russia's famous wooden nesting dolls are called Fabergé eggs.
statements.truth: The nesting dolls are called matryoshka dolls. Fabergé eggs are jewelled eggs made for the Russian tsars.

statements.text: Oymyakon, a village in Siberia, is one of the coldest inhabited places on Earth.
Poland's Malbork Castle is the largest castle in the world by land area.
Kraków is the capital of Poland.
statements.truth: Warsaw is Poland's capital. Kraków was the capital until around 1600 and is still a big tourist favourite.

statements.text: Composer Frédéric Chopin was born in Poland.
Bislama, Vanuatu's national language, is a dialect of French.
statements.truth: Bislama is a creole language based mostly on English words.

statements.text: Vanuatu has several active volcanoes, including Mount Yasur.
Vanuatu's sand drawings are recognised by UNESCO as a world treasure of culture.
Tulips were grown in the Ottoman Empire, centred on today's Türkiye, before they became famous in the Netherlands.
Cappadocia is famous for hot-air balloon flights over tall rock towers called fairy chimneys.
Turkish delight is a crunchy baked biscuit.
statements.truth: Turkish delight, or lokum, is a soft, chewy sweet made from starch and sugar.
